provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored by an independent agent without access to the tool code; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build and its shipped rule pack.
reference: Pairwise-outcome corpus for a hazard-group chemical storage compatibility matrix. Each case lists a small inventory (name, physical state, CLP/GHS hazard statement codes, optional generic group meaning, optional location) and the expected matrix cell(s) in the README vocabulary X (prohibited together) / S (segregate) / U (unknown - review SDS) / C (no modelled conflict), or a boolean property (not C / not X) where the sources establish only that a pair reacts or must be separated. Expectations come from the CLP hazard-statement texts (EUH031/EUH032/EUH014/H26x/H27x), HSE HSG71 paras 71, 73, 120, the EPA-600/2-80-076 compatibility chart as transcribed by NIH ORF and Rutgers REHS and explained in WIPP Addendum B2, and the acceptance criteria of spec 11 / 00-common (unknown never safe, no inference from product name, symmetry, non-transitivity, rule id per cell, pack version in report). Stated mapping principle: fire, explosion, toxic/flammable gas or 'do not mix' -> X; heat or innocuous gas only -> S. Four randomized inventories (seed 20260916, n = 6/12/20/30) are generated by ref.py. 'group' values are generic meanings the harness maps to the tool's nearest group; null means no group chosen.

tools.petrov.re spec 11 Chemical Compatibility & Storage Matrix (MVP, model rules, results, QA, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common section 0.5
Case generator and count/property evaluator: bench/chemicalstorage/ref.py (stdlib, seed 20260916)
tolerance: All checks are categorical or integer and compared exactly: the tool is a rule engine with no numerical model, so there is no physical scale to set a tolerance from. Two non-scalar forms are used in the inventory cases: 'exact-subset' (every listed pair must have the stated cell; unlisted pairs are unconstrained because no source was read for them) and 'lower-bound' (count must be at least ref). Where the sources establish only a reaction or a separation duty, the check is the boolean 'not C' rather than a guessed X/S/U.

not_benchmarked.Gas separations: Compressed gas x acid/base/corrosive and gas x non-gas flammable (README CHEM-P-011/012): no source read states these separations.
not_benchmarked.Toxic and pyrophoric: Toxic x flammable (CHEM-P-013) and pyrophoric x any (CHEM-P-008): HSG71 paras read describe pyrophorics but do not state a separation from all others; no case.
not_benchmarked.Combustible organics: Oxidiser x combustible non-flammable organic (CHEM-P-002): 'combustible organic' cannot be expressed from hazard codes and the group list was not seen.
not_benchmarked.Flammable with acid or base: Flammable x non-oxidising acid and flammable x base: the LA County fact sheet lists these families as incompatible, EPA 1 x 101 was transcribed only once (H, G); sources conflict with general practice, so no expectation is set.
not_benchmarked.Caustic with oxidiser: Caustic x oxidiser (EPA 10 x 104 transcribed once as H, G) - not confirmed.
not_benchmarked.Exceptions on prohibited pairs: Exceptions with a source on an X pair: spec 11 allows an explicit exception source to override the most conservative rule; README says X is never lowered. Not benchmarked either way.
not_benchmarked.Exact outcome of reactive pairs: Exact outcome (X vs S vs U) for organic peroxide x acid/base and water-reactive x non-aqueous partners: only 'not C' asserted.
not_benchmarked.Unread source tables: HSG71 Table 2 cells and TRGS 510 Tabelle 2 cells: could not be read (extraction failed / 403).
not_benchmarked.Outside the MVP scope: Quantity limits, jurisdiction packs, secondary-containment wording, PDF layout, localisation, permalink, pictograms: out of spec MVP or not a compatibility claim.
not_benchmarked.Inventory size limit: Maximum inventory size above 30 entries: the limit is a README property, not a spec requirement.
